title: Deprecate `fixcm=True` in `Langevin` in favor of `FixCom` to get correct distributions both for positions and momenta
body:
(EDIT: 2026-02-22)

# Summary

This MR solves #1871 by ~using `FixCom` internally~ deprecating `fixcm=True` in `Langevin` in favor of asking users to set `FixCom` by themselves explicitly.

closes #1871

# Details

~Instead of shifting and scaling `rnd_pos` and `rnd_vel`, the present MR attaches internally `FixCom` before the updates of positions/momenta and then removes it.~

~This is done at every MD step. This might look ugly. It is, however, necessary not to just attach `FixCom` to `atoms` in e.g. `__init__` and leave it, because:~

~1. Except inside `Langevin`, we do not want it to affect e.g. several `Atoms` methods (`set_positions()`, `get_forces()`, `get_temperature()`, etc.), unless users explicitly attach `FixCom` beforehand by themselves.~

~2. After the instantization of `Langevin`, it is possible that users do something they want using the above `Atoms` methods before `run`.~

~The approach in the present MR should be safe even when users set `FixCom` beforehand while with `fixcm=True` (although it is not particularly encouraged). This will just do redundant operations to fix the COM position and velocity.~

~There is a potential conflict with the internal `FixCom` and the other user-attached constraints. This is however the issue not specifically for `Langevin` but a present general restriction of ASE (cf. #1836). I therefore think this should be addressed in a separate MR.~

~The present MR seemingly reproduces #1285 when `fixcm=True`. I now think this is "as expected", because, without `FixCom` attached, `atoms.get_temeprature()` cannot know if `Langevin` has run with or without fixing the COM and therefore cannot know how much the DOF to be reduced.
For this, it is still recommended to use `fixcm=False` together with `FixCom` explicitly attached by the users.
To make this clear for users, the docstring is updated as follows.~

(EDIT: 2026-02-22) Figure removed to avoid confusion.

(EDIT: 2026-02-22) Instead of the above, the MR now suggests simply deprecating `fixcm=True` (as the first step, raising `UserWarning`). The final goal is to remove `fixcm` entirely from `Langevin`. For this, several deprecation steps will be taken. (1) Asking users to set `fixcm=False`. (2) `fixcm=False` will be the default and raise an error for `fixcm=True`. (3) Raise warning when `fixcm` is used. (4) Complete removal of `fixcm`.

Two tests are substantially added or modified, in order not to reproduce the issues reported in #1871 in future anymore (hopefully).

- `test_nvt_npt.py`: Most of the changes are just refactoring. In addition, it also tests if the standard deviation of instant temperatures agrees with the one expected from the corresponding gamma distribution.

- `test_position_distribution.py` checks if the distance distribution of a Morse potential in NVT is reproduced, by comparing the the probability distribution functions based on the KL divergence. While it is so far only for `Langevin`, in principle we can test also other NVT thermostats.

@askhl May I ask your review? Also, feedbacks from users/developers are very much appreciated, particularly those in #1871, @timduignan, @AndrewRosen, @thomasloux, @tgmaxson, @schiotz, @drFaustroll

author: yuzie007

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: Before we merge this, I would like to see how it interacts with Asap.  I suspect it may require some changes in Asap, and perhaps that requires minor changes here as well.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I'm not enormously happy that we modify the constraints as we go along, but I suppose it'll work so okay :sweat_smile: .

We should however do try/finally here so the popping is guaranteed also if there's an error (which someone might catch).

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I think this is how we should do it:

 * If `self.fix_com` and atoms.constraints is *not* empty in the beginning, raise an error
 * If at the end, `atoms.constraints` is anything except a one-element list containing our own constraint, raise an error

Then it should be safe.

comments.author: tgmaxson
comments.body:
@askhl Can't there be other constraints involved?  I can imagine a Hookean constraint for example wanting to be applied during MD or something to steer MD.  That corner case should be handled.

- If `self.fix_com` is True and `atoms.constraints` already contains the `FixCOM` constraint, raise an error.
- If `self.fix_com` is True and `atoms.constraints` does not contain the `FixCOM` constraint, we apply it temporarily during the MD steps.  The constraint can be held internally on the Langevin class.
- If `self.fix_com` is None (default) and `atoms.constraints` already contains the `FixCOM` constraint, the user created the `FixCOM` manually.
- If `self.fix_com` is False and `atoms.constraints` already contains the `FixCOM` constraint, the user created the `FixCOM` manually and we should raise a warning to make sure they get the intended behavior.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
We don't know whether the fixcom constraint in combination with other constraints produces the right thermodynamics, or even whether different kinds of constraints work together at all, thermodynamics or not.

We should not try to do something automatically which we suspect to produce wrong results.

The user can set up the constraints manually (and bear the burden of testing them) if it's going to be advanced.

comments.author: tgmaxson
comments.body:
I think I can agree with that.  It would be nice if we somehow had a master list of constraints which do / dont work with other constraints to throw this warning for non-expert users which might accidently manually construct this though.

I then suggest that a secondary flag be added to let constraints work with the fix_com in langevin for expert users that disables the error.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
The way to constrain things in ASE (for better or worse) is to set up the constraints and attach them to the Atoms.

Then Langevin (for some reason) added a shortcut to make that slightly easier in one case.  But then it turned out to produce wrong results.  So we could either remove the shortcut, or fix it.  But I don't think we should be adding *more keywords* inside Langevin to for additional control over constraints, because that does not allow doing anything that cannot already be done with the Atoms in the standard way.  We don't have a reason to add these same or similar keywords to NEB, optimizer, Dimer method, minima hopping, etc., where one might also want to constrain things.  We'd accumulate a lot of keywords with code and special cases that we need to test, document, and maintain, all to solve a problem that the user can solve before creating those objects.

comments.author: tgmaxson
comments.body: Then honestly, I am somewhat in the belief that this option of Langevin should just raise an error and do nothing and report to the user what the right approach actually would be, as it should be immediately deprecated.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
I think I am tempted to agree with @tgmaxson here: Let's follow the fundamental principle of engineering: KISS ("Keep it simple, stupid").  Lets remove the fixcm option.

Unfortunately, this breaks backwards compatibility in a nasty way, since it silently will stop fixing the center-of-mass per default, and that is bad.

So let's remove this option in a disruptive way: In this version of ASE (3.28.0b1 **and** the final 3.28.0) we keep the default ``fixcm=True``, but if Langevin is called with the default it aborts with an error like this

```
The fixcm option of Langevin is broken, do not use it (it is on per default)!
* If you want to keep the center of mass fixed, use the FixCom constraint
  on the atoms, and specify fixcm=None when you call Langevin.
* If you want the center of mass to drift thermally, just specify fixcm=False.
```

In a later version we turn fixcm off per default.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body:
I would be okay with a noisy error forcing everyone to update the code, since we are not really breaking things when those things were (very unfortunately) already broken.

One issue brought up by @schiotz is that if we attach a temporary constraint, then someone afterwards call `atoms.get_temperature()` and it will be subtly wrong because the constraint is no longer there.  (It would *always* have been subtly wrong since fixcm wasn't based on an actual constraint).

So the "most correct" solution seems to be:

 * Add a warning to force everyone to set fixcm=False explicitly (with deprecation period)
 * Then force everyone to *not* set fixcm and remove the parameter (another deprecation period)

The "least painful" solution is probably:

 * Deprecate the parameter immediately and change the default behaviour willy-nilly so it does not attempt to constrain anything.  After all, people doing MD normally have a thousand atoms, so the error is not huge (which is why these errors can hide).  We'd still list this clearly as a breaking change.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @askhl, @schiotz, @tgmaxson for the discussion!

> One issue brought up by @schiotz is that if we attach a temporary constraint, then someone afterwards call atoms.get_temperature() and it will be subtly wrong because the constraint is no longer there. (It would always have been subtly wrong since fixcm wasn't based on an actual constraint).

Yes, it will seemingly reproduce the issue #1285. So, to have a correct temperature from `get_temperature()` we need anyway `fixcm=False` either with or without `FixCom`.

Reading the discussion above, it looks we are more or less going to remove `fixcm` entirely (either with or without deprecation periods). I also agree on this, and I also think this is the simplest way, both for ASE and ASAP.

Regarding "most correct" or "least painful", I am in principle fine with both, but I think the "most correct" solution will be much less surprising for users (I mean, users have chance to know how to fix and get the correct behavior). I can take care of the deprecation period for every ASE release until complete `fixcm` removal. I will update the MR in this afternoon.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
I have updated the MR to simply deprecate `fixcm=True`. The MR title and the description have revised.

@askhl @schiotz @tgmaxson Could you have a look again? Is this the way to go, or at least closer to it?

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
Just a nitpick: The variable ``_`` is normally used to signify "this return value will not be used".  But here you actually use it.  What about calling it ``attrib`` or just ``a`` instead.

I suppose the change was because the line was too long.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @schiotz for the review! The change is indeed to make them in one line, and I agree on not using `_` but something else.

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body:
> Is this the way to go, or at least closer to it?

@yuzie007: I think this is exactly the way to go.  Well done, I'll begin adapting Asap to reflect this.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Maybe we should clarify this since the error is small when there are many atoms, as opposed to "all results are garbage"

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @askhl, I fully agree with you! I have now revised the description to be more precise.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @schiotz and @askhl for the suggestions! Following them, I have updated the MR.

comments.author: timduignan
comments.body: Thanks for fixing! I agree with this approach.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: Fantastic, thanks a lot @yuzie007!

comments.author: schiotz
comments.body: Yes, thanks a lot to all the contributors to this one!  Great to finally get it done right.
